title: Rast wins at the Red Bull Ring after Juncadella's restart penalty
dek: René Rast won Race 1 at the Red Bull Ring for Audi from ninth on the grid after pole-sitter Daniel Juncadella, leading late on, was given a 30-second restart penalty and dropped to 14th.

chapters.title: A title fight with two rounds left
text: The DTM arrived at the Red Bull Ring for the ninth of its ten rounds with the championship down to three names. Gary Paffett led the standings for Mercedes-AMG, with his team-mate Paul di Resta right behind, while the defending champion René Rast sat third after sweeping both races at the Nürburgring two weeks earlier. Rast said the Audi camp now had nothing to lose, though he admitted the gap to the two Mercedes drivers was still large.

The other talking point was a seventh Mercedes. Five-time World Rally champion Sébastien Ogier made his DTM debut as a guest starter in the #17 car, after the DMSB waived the rule that kept the field to six cars per manufacturer and Audi and BMW agreed to it. He had tested the car at Vallelunga in August and said he would keep his expectations realistic, since a DTM weekend was nothing like a rally.
Philipp Eng and Lucas Auer, the two Austrians in the field, were racing at home. After a dry Friday, rain overnight left the track wet on Saturday morning and the forecast promised more of it.

chapters.title: Juncadella takes pole in the wet
text: Qualifying began in heavy rain and was red-flagged after five minutes, with puddles and aquaplaning making the hilly circuit too dangerous. The break lasted roughly twelve minutes, and when the rain eased the lap times fell quickly.

Pole looked set to be settled between two former Formula 1 drivers, di Resta and Timo Glock, until Daniel Juncadella put his Mercedes on top with a 1:36.071. Glock's final lap brought him to within 0.071 seconds of the Spaniard, who took his third pole of the season. Mike Rockenfeller was third for Audi, 0.229 seconds off the pace, with di Resta fourth on 1:36.534 and Marco Wittmann the next best, fifth for BMW.

Lucas Auer was sixth, Augusto Farfus seventh and Robin Frijns eighth. Rast could manage only ninth, and Paffett, who was among several drivers to run through the gravel at the Turn 6 left-hander, was tenth. Ogier, in his first DTM qualifying, was last of the 19 cars, 2.889 seconds slower than Juncadella.

chapters.title: Chaos at the first corners
text: The track was still damp at the start but the racing line had dried, and Juncadella led away from pole with Rockenfeller passing Glock for second. Behind them the opening corners turned messy: Frijns's Audi was spun around, Loïc Duval's car was caught up in it and Paffett, directly behind, could not avoid hitting the Frenchman. Duval was out at the end of the lap, Frijns pitted with damage and Paffett dropped to the back of the field, behind even Ogier.

The safety car came out to clear debris and stayed out for about four laps. Because of the damp conditions the restart was a normal single-file one, and Rockenfeller took the lead from Juncadella, who ran wide while defending at Turn 3.

chapters.title: Juncadella back in front
text: Juncadella used DRS to retake the lead by around lap 15 and, once the mandatory stops had cycled through, he held a gap of about three seconds over Rockenfeller. Nico Müller and Rast had gained places in the stop phase and found themselves in a train behind Wittmann, who was third. Together with di Resta they fought a spectacular battle for the last podium place.

Further back Paffett fought his way through the field, scrapping with Frijns, Eng and Pascal Wehrlein just outside the points, while Ogier, on cold tyres after his stop, spun but kept going. The race looked settled until Glock’s BMW came to a halt at Turn 9 and brought out the safety car for the second time.

chapters.title: A penalty, a swap and a win for Rast
text: With three laps left the field lined up two by two for an Indy-style restart, Juncadella leading Rockenfeller, Müller and Rast. The Spaniard crawled round to set the pace, survived the green flag and was 1.2 seconds clear as the final lap began, only for the stewards to give him a drive-through penalty for accelerating too early. There was no time to serve it, so it became 30 seconds, which sent him from the front of the field to 14th. Juncadella said he had stayed within the allowed speed range of 60 to 80 km/h and called the decision part of how the series was "digging its own grave". At the restart Müller had also passed Wittmann for third, and Wittmann slid down to seventh.

Rockenfeller now led, but Audi had a different plan. Müller and then Rockenfeller let Rast, who was ahead of both in the championship, through in the closing corners, and he took the flag 2.8 seconds behind Juncadella on the road to win his third race in a row. Rockenfeller finished 0.705 seconds back and Müller 0.887. Rast called it no real victory, saying Rockenfeller deserved it, but added that it was good for the title fight.

Di Resta was fourth, 1.153 seconds behind, ahead of Jamie Green and Auer, and Paffett salvaged a single point in tenth. Di Resta took the championship lead on 216 points and Rast moved to 174, 42 behind with 84 still available. Fritz called the day a lost one for Mercedes.

facts.v: Juncadella was given a drive-through penalty for a restart infringement with three laps remaining; with no time to serve it, it was converted to 30 seconds and he was classified 14th.
Juncadella took pole with a 1:36.071 in a red-flagged wet session, 0.071 seconds ahead of Glock.
